title: Tourist Season, 2007
logline: The first tourist who's come to Small Wood because of the strip. Not the helicopter. The dog. Wood doesn't know what to do with that.

panels.composition: Gully's. A young TOURIST with a printout — not the parody; 'Barnaby at Eight,' the July Sunday. Holding it toward WOOD.

characters.pose: holding a printout of the Sunday

balloons.text: I drove from Spokane. For the beach in this. Is it here? Is it a real beach?

image.prompt: a young tourist holding a printout of a five-tier watercolor comic page toward a thin man on a shop stool, a dog, a man in an apron, muddy flats

panels.composition: Wood, looking at his own Sunday in a stranger's hands.

balloons.text: ...It's at the end of the road. Left at the log.

image.prompt: close-up of a thin man looking at his own comic page held by a stranger, unsure of his face

panels.composition: Gully, from the machine, not looking.

balloons.text: Tide's out at four. Take the dog.

image.prompt: a man in an apron speaking without looking up from an espresso machine

panels.composition: The beach. The tourist, WOOD, and BARNABY walking the length of it, the tourist holding the printout up against the real thing. It matches. Wood behind, not drawing.

characters.pose: holding the printout up to the beach

image.prompt: a tourist holding a printed watercolor comic page up against a real beach that matches it, a thin man walking behind and a dog ahead, no words

art.line: brush-pen scanned; muddy digital flats; Sundays in watercolor, improving
art.palette: limited, muddy; Sundays gray-green, rust, one warm

notes: Someone drove from Spokane for the beach in the strip. It matches.
